question: Radioactivity occurs in unstable nuclei. Explain how the balance between nuclear force and electrostatic repulsion affects nuclear stability.

options.A: A nucleus is stable when electrostatic repulsion is greater than the nuclear force; otherwise it never decays.
options.B: Radioactivity is independent of nuclear force and electrostatic repulsion.
options.C: Nuclear force and electrostatic repulsion are both attractive, so heavy nuclei are always stable.
options.D: Short-range nuclear force attracts nucleons, while protons repel electrostatically. A nucleus is stable when nuclear attraction sufficiently balances the proton repulsion; if the balance is inadequate, the nucleus may be unstable and decay toward a more stable state.
